title: Water Treatment PLC Overpressure & Valve Tampering
mitreId: T0836: Modify Parameter / T0855: Unauthorized Command

attackIngress.origin: Compromised Field Technician Laptop via Vendor Maintenance VPN
attackIngress.entryPath: External Internet -> Municipal VPN Gateway -> IT/OT DMZ -> Water VLAN 12 (10.240.12.0/24)
attackIngress.technique: Lateral Movement & Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) ARP Poisoning targeting Modbus TCP Port 502

maliciousPayload.injectedValue: 1000 kPa (10.0 Bar) [Factory Safety Limit: 450 kPa / 4.5 Bar]

detectionEngine.method: Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) + Industrial Process Anomaly Sensor
detectionEngine.triggerRule: RULE-ICS-WTR-402: Modbus FC16 Write from unauthorized IP 192.168.88.204 to Safety Register 40104
detectionEngine.telemetryAnomaly: Pressure derivative dP/dt exceeded 1.6 Bar/sec threshold; physical hydraulic pressure surged from 4.2 Bar to 9.85 Bar within 4 seconds

awarenessLesson.coreConcept: IT vs. OT Security & Lack of Native SCADA Encryption
awarenessLesson.analystGuideline: Legacy Modbus protocols have ZERO built-in authentication or encryption. Any device on the subnet can inject arbitrary setpoints. Analysts must never simply kill power—abrupt pump shutdown causes water hammer pipe ruptures. Mechanical pressure relief bypass MUST be verified first!

potentialImpact: Catastrophic pipeline rupture risk at North Reservoir; Potential contaminated water surge or civic drinking water loss for 250,000 residents; Structural damage estimated at ₹4.2 Crore.
anomalyEvidence: Modbus TCP Function Code 0x10 (Write Multiple Registers) injected from unauthenticated IP 192.168.88.204
Overpressure setpoint register 40104 altered from 4.5 Bar to 10.0 Bar
Safety interlock relay heartbeat missed for 3 consecutive cycles (timeout 1500ms)
Unsynchronized firmware checksum delta detected on PLC Controller EEPROM

playbook.title: Zero-Trust Device Isolation
playbook.description: Quarantine PLC-WTR-01 Ethernet interface from the OT supervisory network to sever remote malicious Modbus commands.

playbook.title: Activate Mechanical Fail-Safe Bypass
playbook.description: Trigger physical pneumatic pressure relief valve (PRV) bypass to drop pipeline pressure safely below 5.0 Bar.

playbook.title: Dispatch Rapid Response Team & CERT-In Notification
playbook.description: Notify City Chief Water Works Engineer, Emergency Municipal Duty Officer, and submit automated incident alert to CERT-In OT Cell.
playbook.team: State Water SCADA Response Unit & CERT-In OT Security Team

playbook.title: Cryptographic Hash & Forensics Preservation
playbook.description: Capture PCAP traffic dump of rogue Modbus frames, calculate SHA-256 evidence hash, and lock audit log for legal compliance.

playbook.title: Verify Public Water Supply Continuity
playbook.description: Confirm automated failover to Gravity Reservoir Feed Ring C to guarantee uninterrupted clean water supply to hospitals and households.

continuityPlan: Secondary gravity feed lines automatically engage at 3.5 Bar. Zero downtime in drinking water distribution. Civic advisory not required.

title: Arterial Traffic Signal MitM & All-Green Collision Exploit
mitreId: T0803: Block Command Message / T0816: Device Modification

attackIngress.origin: Rogue Cellular 4G LTE Tap physically spliced into roadside signal cabinet
attackIngress.entryPath: Physical lock bypass on roadside cabinet -> RJ45 Ethernet tap into Managed Industrial Switch Port 4
attackIngress.technique: Unauthenticated SNMP/NTCIP 1202 broadcast packet injection over UDP Port 161

detectionEngine.method: Hardware Conflict Monitor Unit (CMU) Voltage Interlock + SNMP Traffic Anomaly Monitor
detectionEngine.triggerRule: RULE-CMU-CONFLICT-01: Conflicting dual green voltage detected on Signal Field Terminals 2 & 4
detectionEngine.telemetryAnomaly: Cycle time dropped from 90s to 10s deadlock; CMU hardware interlock relay tripped at 10:31:02

awarenessLesson.coreConcept: Physical Safety Interlocks in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)
awarenessLesson.analystGuideline: In traffic systems, software cannot be trusted alone. Signal cabinets use an analog, hardwired Conflict Monitor Unit (CMU). When an exploit forces dual green lights, the CMU must automatically trip to Flashing Amber to prevent catastrophic high-speed arterial collisions.

potentialImpact: Severe multi-vehicle collision hazard at major 4-way arterial intersection (Mahatma Gandhi Marg); Total gridlock on designated Civil Hospital emergency ambulance corridor.
anomalyEvidence: Unauthorized UDP NTCIP broadcast packets on port 161 (SNMPv1 community string bypass attempt)
Phase hold override command forced green signals on both North-South and East-West corridors simultaneously
Hardware Conflict Monitor Unit (CMU) triggered safety trip circuit at 10:31:02
Packet origin traced to unauthorized rogue Wi-Fi/4G dongle connected to roadside signal cabinet

playbook.title: Force Hardware Conflict Monitor Flashing Amber
playbook.description: Engage hardware interlock relay to force all intersection signal faces into Flashing Yellow / Amber cautionary mode.

playbook.title: Quarantine Controller Roadside Switch Port
playbook.description: Remotely disable physical switch port on OT Ring Switch #4 to sever attacker access from roadside cabinet tap.

playbook.title: Dispatch Traffic Police Patrol & Field Technician
playbook.description: Send urgent high-priority dispatch to City Traffic Control Room for manual officer traffic direction and cabinet inspection.
playbook.team: City Traffic Police Control Room & ITMS Rapid Field Team

playbook.title: Reroute Emergency Ambulances to Secondary Corridor
playbook.description: Switch V2X emergency green corridor to bypass Junction 4 via Nehru Bridge arterial route.

playbook.title: Generate Forensic Timeline & Police Report
playbook.description: Compile packet capture and CCTV timestamp to file cyber intrusion FIR with State Cyber Police Division.

continuityPlan: Signal hardware failsafe guarantees flashing yellow default within 200ms. Traffic flow slows safely without catastrophic collision.

title: Substation 11kV Feeder DNP3 Relay Trip Attack
mitreId: T0855: Unauthorized Command / T0831: Manipulation of Control

attackIngress.origin: Stolen Substation Remote Access Gateway Credentials (Phished Subcontractor)
attackIngress.entryPath: Vendor Remote Telemetry Link -> SCADA Substation Gateway -> Substation Process Bus (IEC 61850 / DNP3)

maliciousPayload.protocol: DNP3 (Distributed Network Protocol 3) over TCP Port 20000
maliciousPayload.registerTarget: Control Relay Output Block (CROB) Object 12, Variation 1, Index 3 (Feeder Trip)
maliciousPayload.injectedValue: Force Breaker OPEN (Trip 11kV Feeder 4 to Civil Hospital)

detectionEngine.method: Network Behavior Analysis (NBA) for SCADA Protocols + IEC 61850 Dissector
detectionEngine.triggerRule: RULE-DNP3-SBO-FLOOD: Burst of 75 unauthenticated trip commands within 1000ms
detectionEngine.telemetryAnomaly: 11kV busbar voltage plummeted to 9.4 kV; grid frequency jittered to 48.70 Hz; feeder breaker forced OPEN

awarenessLesson.coreConcept: Substation Cyber Defense & Industrial Protocol Cryptography
awarenessLesson.analystGuideline: Power substations are high-value targets (similar to Ukraine 2015/2016 attacks). Modern substations require IEC 62351 cryptographic authentication. Analysts must immediately isolate the rogue process bus and verify hospital Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS) activate diesel/solar microgrids.

potentialImpact: Loss of grid power to Civil Hospital, District Data Center, and Northern Municipal Water Filtration facility; Potential surge damage to industrial microgrids.
anomalyEvidence: Burst of 75 unauthorized DNP3 Select-Before-Operate (SBO) command packets directed at Object 12 Point 3 (Feeder Breaker Trip)
Source IP: 10.240.30.98 (Unauthorized device on OT Substation LAN)
Authentication token header missing cryptographic signature required by IEEE 1686
Rapid voltage dip observed across Busbar 2

playbook.title: Block Rogue Substation MAC Address
playbook.description: Issue 802.1X quarantine rule on Ruggedcom switch port to terminate rogue device connection.

playbook.title: Activate Hospital Island Microgrid & Diesel Generators
playbook.description: Trigger automated ATS (Automatic Transfer Switch) to maintain uninterrupted power to ICU, NICU, and operating theaters.

playbook.title: Alert State Electricity Transmission Utility
playbook.description: Contact Chief Load Dispatcher (SLDC) and Substation Duty Engineer for physical key-lock verification before manual breaker reclose.
playbook.team: State Electricity Discom Grid SOC & Substation Physical Security

playbook.title: Log SCADA Event Sequence of Events (SOE)
playbook.description: Record millisecond-accurate SOE logs into secure immutable audit vault for root cause analysis.

continuityPlan: Hospital ATS transfer engages in 1.4 seconds. Solar microgrid switches to island mode to power emergency communications.

title: Emergency 112 Dispatch Server DDoS & API Exhaustion
category: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) & Syn Flood
mitreId: T0814: Denial of Service / T0813: Denial of Control

attackIngress.origin: Global Mirai-variant IoT Botnet (Spoofed ASNs across 3,200 IP nodes)
attackIngress.entryPath: Public Internet -> City BGP Gateway -> Load Balancer Cluster -> Dispatch Application Pool
attackIngress.technique: Volumetric TCP SYN Flood on Port 443 + Layer-7 HTTP POST Flooding on /api/v1/dispatch

maliciousPayload.registerTarget: Application Thread Backlog & Postgres Connection Pool

detectionEngine.method: NetFlow Volumetric Threshold Monitoring + Web Application Firewall (WAF)
detectionEngine.triggerRule: RULE-WAF-DDOS-09: Inbound HTTP request rate > 5000 req/sec with anomalous user-agents
detectionEngine.telemetryAnomaly: CPU utilization surged to 98.4%; TCP backlog queue saturated; database latency spiked from 14ms to 3,400ms

awarenessLesson.analystGuideline: Emergency 112 services cannot afford even 30 seconds of downtime. SOC analysts must quickly reroute ingress BGP routing through upstream DDoS scrubbing centers and activate failover to air-gapped copper/PSTN CAD workstations.

potentialImpact: Citizens unable to connect to 112 emergency police, fire, and ambulance dispatch; Web call-taking consoles experiencing 18-second freezes.
anomalyEvidence: Volumetric SYN Flood exceeding 4.2 Gbps originating from 3,200 external botnet IPs targeting port 443
HTTP POST flood directed at /api/v1/dispatch/create-emergency endpoint with malformed JSON payloads
Server connection backlog pool depleted to 0 available worker threads
Geo-location analysis reveals spoofed source ASNs

playbook.title: Engage Upstream Cloudflare / BGP Scrubbing Center
playbook.description: Reroute public DNS traffic through National Scrubbing Center to filter malicious botnet SYN packets.

playbook.title: Failover to Backup Dedicated Fiber CAD Standby
playbook.description: Shift active 112 call-takers to encrypted dedicated fiber-optic CAD intranet hot standby cluster.

playbook.title: Notify Police Cyber Crime Cell & ISP Tier-1 NOC
playbook.description: Issue emergency abuse report with IP packet dumps to upstream telecom providers for upstream rate-limiting.
playbook.team: Police Command Telecom Bureau & National Internet Exchange

playbook.title: Audit Log Forensics & Attack Vector Fingerprinting
playbook.description: Archive WAF access logs, request signatures, and bot user-agent profiles for cyber investigation.

continuityPlan: Dedicated PSTN/ISDN copper emergency trunk lines remain 100% operational. Hot standby cluster restores 112 web CAD within 30 seconds.

title: Smart Streetlight LoRaWAN Gateway Credential Brute-Force
mitreId: T0812: Default Credentials / T0866: Exploitation of Remote Services

attackIngress.origin: Internet-exposed SSH port (22) left active on Edge Streetlight Gateway pole
attackIngress.entryPath: Cellular WAN IP -> Linux SSH Daemon on Edge Gateway -> Attempted VLAN Hopping to SCADA
attackIngress.technique: Dictionary Credential Stuffing & Default Password Guessing ('admin/admin', 'root/root')

detectionEngine.method: Host-Based Intrusion Detection (HIDS) + Edge Firewall Syslog Parser
detectionEngine.triggerRule: RULE-HIDS-SSH-BURST: More than 10 failed SSH attempts in 60s from untrusted WAN IP
detectionEngine.telemetryAnomaly: CPU load spiked from 8% to 65% due to cryptographic handshakes; street illumination telemetry dropped to 5 lux

awarenessLesson.coreConcept: IoT Device Hardening & Zero-Trust Network Segmentation
awarenessLesson.analystGuideline: IoT devices are frequently deployed with default credentials. If compromised, attackers use them as bridgeheads to pivot into critical Water or Power networks. Analysts must isolate the gateway and verify robust VLAN segmentation.

potentialImpact: Streetlights across Zone 4 could be turned off causing nighttime road hazards; Gateway could be used as an entry bridge into municipal SCADA intranet.
anomalyEvidence: 1,480 failed SSH (port 22) password attempts within 3 minutes targeting user 'admin' and 'root'
Outbound connection detected on TCP port 4444 to known Mirai command-and-control IP
High rate of unauthenticated LoRa Join-Requests with duplicate DevEUI keys
Network segmentation firewall blocked unauthorized lateral ping to 10.240.12.10 (Water PLC)

playbook.title: Quarantine Gateway WAN & Disable Remote SSH
playbook.description: Drop external WAN routing for GW-IOT-99 and disable remote SSH daemon via local console command.

playbook.title: Engage Autonomous Astronomical Clock Fallback
playbook.description: Switch streetlights to autonomous astronomical timer so lights stay turned on regardless of gateway status.

playbook.title: Assign IoT Security Patching Work Order
playbook.description: Schedule mandatory firmware upgrade, rotate private LoRa AppKey credentials, and enforce certificate-based SSH.
playbook.team: Smart City IoT Operations & Vendor Security Support

playbook.title: Record Incident Log Entry
playbook.description: Document failed brute-force vectors and confirm no lateral penetration occurred into Water or Traffic VLANs.

continuityPlan: Streetlights remain powered on via local photocell/clock sensors. Zero blackout on public roads.
